code:
$ docker exec catalog-db sh -c 'echo saved > /var/lib/postgresql/data/test.txt'
$ docker rm -f catalog-db
$ docker run -d --name catalog-db postgres:16
$ docker exec catalog-db cat /var/lib/postgresql/data/test.txt
cat: ...test.txt: No such file or directory
caption: A fresh container starts from the image's original filesystem -- every write inside the old one is gone with it.

eyebrow: Named volumes: Docker-managed, outside the container's lifecycle
code:
$ docker volume create catalog-db-data

$ docker run -d --name catalog-db \
  -v catalog-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:16

$ docker rm -f catalog-db
$ docker run -d --name catalog-db \
  -v catalog-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:16
caption: The container is disposable -- catalog-db-data isn't. The new container mounts the same volume and sees every row the old one wrote.

eyebrow: Bind mounts: a host path, mapped straight in
caption: Local development: a host source directory mounted into the container, so edits on the host show up inside instantly.
